_comment: Release notes shown by cop after an update (what's new since the user's previous version, including skipped versions). 'approved' MUST be true before a version's features are shown to users and before that version is released. When cutting a release, add an entry for the new version, review the features, then set approved=true.

features: cop help and reference.html now render `type X = Base & { ... }` fields; all six `:as<Language>` narrowings are documented and linked.
`:as<Language>` narrowing now applies to Methods and Statements across all 6 languages; added a flat `codebase.Methods` collection.
`cop init --checks`: generate cop checks from your repo's existing instructions via a coding agent.
`cop verify` now statically type-checks call arguments (e.g. flags anchoring `toError` on a non-position before runtime).
Package auto-restore now repairs incomplete/stale cached packages instead of looping on "restored ok" / "not found".
Running a package now uses `cop run <package>`; a mistyped or unknown command shows a clear error (with a suggestion) instead of trying to restore it as a package.
New `sameAs` / `sm` functions: convention-insensitive identifier comparison (ignores case, underscores, and hyphens).
cop now checks once a day for a newer release and shows a persistent reminder to run `cop update`.
After you update, cop prints a concise "what's new" summary — including any versions you skipped.

New built-in analysis for config formats and scripts: YAML (CI workflows, Kubernetes, docker-compose), Dockerfile, XML (.csproj/pom.xml), OpenAPI, SQL, Bash, and PowerShell — each with a ready-to-run check package.
New cross-language SQL injection check flags database queries built from non-constant strings (Python and JavaScript).
TypeScript: `.tsx`/`.jsx` files are now analyzed and `interface`/`enum` declarations are modeled as types.
Language fixes: a `!somePredicate` predicate body and `:any`/`:all`/`:none`/`:count(item ...)` inline expressions now evaluate correctly.
Language fixes: string interpolation now evaluates expressions like `{1 + 2}`; `match` supports the `_` wildcard and case-insensitive arms; verbatim strings `@'\bx\b'` work for regex.

Documented string and object features now work: `.Lower`/`.Upper`/`.Normalized`/`.Words`, object `.Get`/`.Keys`/`.Values`/`:containsKey` with quoted keys, and list `+` append, `.Distinct`/`.Sum`/`.Min`/`.Max`/`.Average`/`.ElementAt`.
`value:function` now invokes the function on the value (e.g. `5:inc`), curried/free-`item` predicates filter correctly, and `foreach` can chain after `&`.
C# provider: `csharp.parse('path')` returns a Codebase and a single `<TargetFramework>` is captured in `Project.Frameworks`.
`cop verify` no longer reports false duplicates for a package overloading or self-importing its own exports, and `cop init` now sets up Copilot CLI hooks.

Module layering now works across Go, Java, Python, and JavaScript: cop discovers each module and its dependencies (e.g. from `go.mod`) and exposes `Project.Name`/`Project.References`, so the `code-layering` package can flag forbidden cross-module dependencies in every language — not just C#.

`cop init --cop-cmd "<invocation>"`: when cop isn't on your PATH (e.g. you run it through mise), the generated agent files and hooks invoke cop your way instead of assuming `cop` on PATH; cop also hints this when it detects a mise config.

Quieter startup: the once-a-day update reminder and post-update "what's new" summary no longer print before `help`/`--version`/`update` output or before an "unknown command" error — a typo now shows just the error.
`cop update` now skips the download when you're already on the latest release (and says so); use `cop update --force` to reinstall.

A package's coding-agent guidance is now installed automatically: running or restoring a package writes its instructions to `.github/instructions/{package}.instructions.md`, scoped by an `applyTo` glob from the package manifest, so GitHub Copilot and compatible agents pick it up. Placement is idempotent — unchanged files don't churn your working tree.
More documented built-ins now work at runtime: `isError`, `Path`, `Matches`, and `Text`.
Glob matching now supports `**`, `**/`, and `?` wildcards, and the Rust parser understands `use path as alias;`.

The `code` package now also provides `Violation`/`CHECK`/`toError`/`toWarning`/`toInfo` and module-layering helpers (the former `code-analysis` and `code-layering` packages were merged into it) — use `import code`.
Refreshed CLI output: help, usage, and the getting-started screen are now consistent, lower-case, and colorized.
The post-update notice is now a single concise line that links to the full release notes, instead of printing the whole feature list (and no longer shows broken characters on Windows consoles).
Error messages are lower-case, with the `error:` prefix highlighted.
`cop run` with no target now prints a clear usage error instead of silently showing the getting-started screen, and the post-update notice no longer appears before that error.
Removed the misleading post-update "updated to cop … / what's new" startup notice. (The "a new version is available" reminder, shown only when you're actually behind the latest release, stays.)
A bare `cop` (no command) now just shows help — it never runs local .cop files. Run something explicitly with `cop run <package>` or `cop <file.cop>`.
Every command now has detailed help: `cop <command> -h` (e.g. `cop run -h`, `cop init -h`) shows that command's usage, options, and examples. (`cop init -h` previously errored.)
Cleaner `cop -h`: the command list shows key options inline — optional ones in [ ], e.g. `cop run <package> [-t <target>]` — and drops the separate global options section.
Commands and option flags are shown in distinct colors so commands stand out.

Source files that fail to parse are no longer hidden: cop now reports syntax errors as warnings (`path(line,col): error: message`) and still analyzes the rest of the file instead of silently skipping or mis-modeling it — for C# and now Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Go, and Java.

Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Go, and Java are now parsed by real lexer + recursive-descent parsers (replacing the previous line-scanners), improving the accuracy of detected types, methods, statements, and imports.

`cop verify <file.cop>` now verifies the whole program — every `.cop` file in the file's directory, like `cop run` — and flags undefined references (e.g. a typo in `CHECK(...)`) that previously passed verify but failed at runtime.
A bare `cop` (no command) now prints the same full command list as `cop -h`.
Built-in check violations now show the check's name in brackets — e.g. `[var-declarations]` — which is exactly the identifier you subtract to turn that rule off.

Turn off a whole built-in rule by name: `let mine = csharp-checks - var-declarations` (works for the C#, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, and Java check packages), or silence a single line with a `// cop-ignore: <check>` comment.
New `nameof(<identifier>)` language intrinsic returns an identifier's name as a string.
VS Code extension: hovering a list of violations (or the `codebase` binding) no longer shows "unknown", and files no longer lose syntax coloring after a lone `#` comment line.

The extension's IntelliSense and syntax highlighting are now generated from cop's own language definitions (types, keywords, predicates), so they stay in sync as the language evolves instead of drifting and breaking.

VS Code: diagnostics, hover, and autocomplete now come from a built-in cop language server (`cop langserver`), so they match the compiler exactly and update live as you type — instead of a separate in-extension implementation that kept drifting and breaking.
Hovering a list of violations now shows its real type (e.g. [Violation]) instead of "unknown".

Editor stays useful mid-edit: a syntax error in one declaration no longer blanks hover, autocomplete, and go-to-definition for the rest of the file — the language server now recovers and keeps the valid declarations.
Filtering a collection by something that isn't a predicate (e.g. an enum value or a plain let) now fails loudly instead of silently returning nothing, so a typo can't make a check pass by accident.
Hardened internal compiler diagnostics for reliability under concurrent runs.
